items.text: Coaching-centre folklore about attempt limits drifts over time.
Second, your real financial and family runway in months.
That list is not what most people actually need first.
It does not mean your years of preparation were wasted.

Ex-aspirants who have gone through this transition describe a specific pattern: after a few serious attempts, you start feeling like you are "very close," and that feeling makes you want to try just once more, almost regardless of the actual numbers.
None of these paths are a downgrade.
A large share of the UPSC static-GK, reasoning, and general studies syllabus overlaps with state Public Service Commission exams, SSC CGL, and RBI/banking exams.
Aspirants who spent years explaining concepts to themselves and study groups often teach better than people who never had to break a subject down from scratch.
A skill-transfer table cannot tell you which lane fits your actual situation. the four questions narrows the decision down to what genuinely matters for you, in order.
Write down your exact attempt count and the maximum attempts and age ceiling for your category from the table above.
This single step ends most of the vague anxiety, because "I might have one attempt left" and "I genuinely have zero attempts left" call for completely different next moves.

blocks.heading: Practical Plan for the Next 6-12 Months

items.text: Use this rough sequence over the next 6 to 12 months as a working order, not a rigid schedule.
In the first stretch after a failed attempt or a decision to stop, do not make any career decision.
Go through the skill-transfer map on this page item by item and note which ones genuinely describe how you think and work, not which ones sound impressive.
Recent UPSC CSE cycles have recommended under a thousand candidates out of several lakh who appeared for Prelims, a selection rate commonly estimated well under 1%.
A path picked to manage other people's reactions rarely holds up once the initial relief wears off.
No amount of research replaces one real test.
